stem: Two engineers on the Fenwick Analytics team plan to start unrelated Terraform changes on the same day using the same shared repository. What does Terraform's team workflow recommend so their changes do not collide?

choices.text: Have both engineers edit the same branch and reconcile conflicts by hand at the end of the day
Each engineer works on a separate version-control branch for their own change
Have each engineer create a separate branch for their change, but never merge it back into the shared branch for review
Apply each engineer's change directly from their own laptop against the shared account

rationale: Saving changes to separate version-control branches is the practice the team workflow describes for avoiding collisions. Editing the same branch and reconciling by hand invites the exact conflicts branching avoids. Branching per change but never merging back leaves each engineer's work permanently isolated, so it never reaches the shared branch or the review the workflow depends on. Applying independently from separate laptops bypasses the shared review and state process entirely.
